characters.name: Timon
characters.description: A fast-talking, hedonistic meerkat who more often than not gets himself and Pumbaa into whatever trouble of the week is going on. Adaptational Dumbass: He seems to have gotten a lot more clueless and stubborn than in the film. "Brazil Nuts" and "I Don't Bolivia" are the finest examples of this. Adaptational Dye-Job: This Timon has three stripes on his back, but in the films he has five. Badass Adorable: Timon is still a small, cute meerkat, and yet is very clever when outsmarting his foes. Badass Bookworm: He may be tiny, but his cleverness enables him to outsmart vicious predators. Not to mention anger him enough and he will strike back so hard that predators run for their lives.

characters.name: Pumbaa
characters.description: A kind-hearted but gassy warthog who usually serves as the voice of reason between him and Timon. Adaptational Intelligence: Though he is something of an airhead like his “Lion King” counterpart, he is given a fair amount of book-smarts and can quote many facts about geography, literature, and history. Baritone of Strength:Played for Laughsin "Home is Where the Hog Is". During romantic moments with Sharla, Pumbaa puts on a smooth, deep voice reminiscent of a suave action hero - quite the opposite of his normal, somewhat squealy tones. Beware the Nice Ones: Pumbaa may not be big-hearted and not very bright, but he becomes a force to be reckoned with if Timon is in danger or if he's truly angry. For example, in the episode "Guatemala Malarkey", he gets pissed off at Timon for talking him into plundering a cursed ancient temple inhabited by a mummy beetle to find a prized, jewel-encrusted (and very worth a lot of money) Glorious Golden Fruit Fly only to find a worthless fruit fly pin. This gets Timon to admit his fear of angry warthogs. Butt-Monkey: Not as much as Timon, but he definitely has his moments, most famously in the music video "Stand By Me".

characters.name: Simba
characters.description: The Lion King of Pride Lands who was adopted by Timon and Pumbaa in the films the show is based on. He occasionally shows up either as living with them or as the king of Pride Rock. Adaptational Badass: Although a mostly competent fighter in the movies that inspired the show, here he has superhero feats such as blowing away hundreds of heavy animals (including elephants and rhinos) with a single roar and being able to knock down a 40 feet tall monster with a single tackle. Appropriate Animal Attire: He apparently owns a drawer full of clothes, but is never shown wearing them. Brilliant, but Lazy: Though more of a badass than the Simba of the movies, he's also noticeably lazier and spends a lot of time just doing nothing (ironically, just like a real lion, in spite of the cartoonish nature of the show’s universe.) This is especially noticeable in the episodeShake Your Djibouti, with his self-doubt coming across more as an excuse to not have to get up and move. When hedoesget involved, though, he effortlessly takes care of any problem in less than a minute. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He disappears completely after season 2.

characters.name: The Hyena Trio
characters.description: A trio of wacky hyenas. Shenzi is the leader, Banzai is her grouchy Lieutenant, and Ed… is Ed. While their film counterparts teamed up with Scar to take over the Pride Lands, here they are shown just trying to get a good meal. Adaptational Comic Relief: While the versions of them from “The Lion King” are certainly funny, here; they have more cartoonish habits, and are overall far less creepy and moreFunny AnimalUnsympathetic Comedy Protagonists. Adaptational Dumbass: Shenzi, the smartest among the group’sLion Kingcounterparts, goes through a bit of this like not knowing how to spell 'X' in "Cooked Goose" (although it’s highly unlikely that herLion Kingcounterpart was literate to begin with). Adaptational Wimp: Downplayed. They are not quite as menacing as their film counterparts,even showing more of their dimwitted sides at times. That being said, they still have theirnot-so-harmlessmoments, with episodes like "Cooked Goose" and "TV Dinner" showing that they are not ones to be messed with. Amusing Injuries: Shenzi loves giving this to the guys.

characters.name: Zazu
characters.description: A hornbill advisor and majordomo to the reigning King of the Pride Lands. Adaptational Jerkass: Much less of aNice Guythan his “Lion King” counterpart, but he still has a heart, and is only mean because of the pressure he's under from Gopher and the Inspector. He comes off mostly as a frustratedPunch-Clock Hero. A Day in the Limelight: He has two episodes in which he stars. Ascended Extra: Mostly a comic relief character in the movies, but gets someCharacter Focushere. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Is more of a finicky perfectionist than his “Lion King” counterpart, but has a heart.

characters.name: Rafiki
characters.description: The wise mandrill shaman, who is shown to have actual magical powers in this universe. He stars in his own segments called "Rafiki Fables". Adaptational Badass: The original Rafiki is more of a fortune teller. The one in this universe is a full on wizard whose staff has magic powers!

characters.name: Gopher
characters.description: Gopher is Zazu's assistant. A Dog Named "Dog": He's a gopher named Gopher. In Germany it's either anEveryone Calls Him "Barkeep"or aHis Name Really Is "Barkeep"situation. Ascended Extra: Possibly. The only possibly appearance he ever made in the first film was very short, so it's unknown if he is the same character. The Comically Serious: The comedy around him comes from his near lack of expression. Dub Name Change: "Oberst" ("Colonel") in the German version.

characters.name: Scar
characters.description: The evil uncle of Simba and the brother and murderer of King Mufasa in “The Lion King”. Despite being dead, he makes the odd random cameo here and there. The Cameo: This is all his appearances boil down to. Shoo Out the Clowns: Inverted. Being one of Disney’s darkest villains, he’s out of place in a Timon and Pumbaa-centered spin-off. Unexplained Recovery: Despite his death in the movie, he makes a couple of cameos.

characters.name: Quint
characters.description: Quint is Timon and Pumbaa's recurring human nemesis. His role varies in each episode he appears in, although one episode shows two Quints together, which may prove that there is more than one of him. The Bad Guy Wins:In "Yukon Con", his plan on stealing Timon and Pumbaa's gold nugget ends in success, with the duo failing to retrieve it. Though his luck ran out in his next appearance in "How to Beat the High Costa Rica". Con Man: As Cusco Quint in the episode "Yukon Con", where he talks Timon into stealing a gold nugget Pumbaa found, planning that the gold will become his own. Evil Chef: As Culinary Quint, he tries to turn Speedy into a French delicacy. He also traps Timon in the kitchen freezer while he and Pumbaa rescue Speedy. Expy: OfHollywood.Both Tony Craig and Bobs Gannaway worked on 2 Stupid Dogs before creating Timon and Pumbaa.He can also be comparable toElmer Fudd, especially as his "Congo Quint" persona as a hunter.

characters.name: Smolder the Bear
characters.description: A grouchy grizzly bear that Timon and Pumbaa often run into and try toavoid making angry. Bears Are Bad News: Basically exists to make Timon and Pumbaa miserable, but only if they make him angry. Given that we're talking aboutTimonandPumbaa, they inevitably find a way to tick him off. Beary Friendly: As long as he doesn't get ticked off, he's a prettyNice Guy. Crying a River: When he's rejected by his crush in "Stay Away From My Honey!", he's so heartbroken that his tears flood an entire hotel and the surrounding street. Deranged Park Ranger: He works as one in "Ready, Aim, Fire", threatening to eat anyone who dares light a fire in his forest.

characters.name: Speedy the Snail
characters.description: Speedy is a talking and singing snail whom Timon and Pumbaa befriend. Big, Thin, Short Trio: He's the short to Pumbaa's big and Timon's thin. Distressed Dude: All of his appearances lead to him getting kidnapped, leading to Timon and Pumbaa to rescue him. Timon calls him out on this to Pumbaa in "Ocean Commotion". Ironic Name: "How do you like that clever juxtaposition? Giving a snail, a noticeably slow creature, the name 'Speedy'." Predator-Prey Friendship: Makes friends with Timon and Pumbaa when the two initially planned on eating him.They couldn't find it in their hearts to eat himafter realizing he can talk and sing.

characters.name: Fred
characters.description: Fred is a meerkat who was Timon's best friend back at the meerkat colony. He enjoys pulling practical jokes on his friends. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Fred can sometimes pull cruel and humiliating practical jokes on Timon, as shown in "Tanzania Zany", where he makes an injured Timon lie down under a tree with sleeping howler monkeys and tries to get Pumbaa to hit the tree and have the howler monkeys fall on Timon, only for Pumbaa to refuse out of loyalty to his best friend. Despite that, Fred still cares deeply about Timon. Old Friend: He was Timon's original "bestest-best friend" prior to meeting Pumbaa. Pun: Timon's hyena jokes always cracked him up. Surveillance Station Slacker: When the Duke leaves the meerkat colony for the day, Fred is left in charge of the castle. However, instead of doing his job, he goes to the grocery store to get a snack and after convincing Timon that it's his chance to go on a date with Princess Tatiana, he falls asleep on duty until he's woken up by a cobra, who he unintentionally lets in the castle.

characters.name: Boss Beaver
characters.description: Boss Beaver is a cranky, ill-tempered loudmouthed beaver whose working lifestyle is the exact opposite of Timon and Pumbaa's Hakuna Matata lifestyle. Busy Beaver: He lives by a philosophy of working hard. Foil: He is the direct opposite of Timon and Pumbaa: whereas Timon and Pumbaa value relaxation and carefreeness, Boss Beaver values hard work and safety. He even has his own philosophies like Timon and Pumbaa do, being Makuta Hamaka (work really hard), safety first, and you break it, you buy it. Hoist by His Own Petard: His attempt to take full credit for the dam Timon and Pumbaa have built results in him ruining his own reputation when the dam proves to be of sub-standard construction. Hypocrite: For someone with an uptight, disciplinary attitude, Boss Beaver is clearly irresponsible as a parent and neglects his son to the point that the latter is a trouble maker behind his back.

characters.name: Irwin
characters.description: Irwin is an accident-prone clumsy penguin whom Timon and Pumbaa meet and befriend during their trip to Antarctica. Annoying Laugh: Has a snorting sort of laugh. Apologises a Lot: He says that he's sorry every time he causes an accident. It starts to annoy Timon. I Just Want to Have Friends: Making new friends is the main reason he loves cruises. He also gets excited when he befriends Timon and Pumbaa. The Jinx: He's prone to causing accidents to those around him. Timon makes it clear to Pumbaa that they suffer whenever Irwin's around.

characters.name: Cheetata and Cheetato
characters.description: Cheetata and Cheetato are a pair of sophisticated and supercilious cheetahs. They are shown hunting for prey and intimidating their victims. Affably Evil: They’ll threaten and try to eat you but theirmanners remain impeccable. Artistic License – Biology: When first meeting the hyenas in "Cooked Goose", Snenzi, Banzai and Ed are scared of them, even though in real life, spotted hyenas are larger and more powerful than cheetahs and it's the latter who is usually intimidated by the former.Subverted later in the same episode, when the hyena trio realizes that they've been duped and threaten to eat the two cheetahs as revenge.Also, going by the quotes provided, it is implied that they preyed on a rhino and hippo, both of which are too big and powerful for cheetahs to target in reality.Very early in the episode, while stalking a wildebeest, the cheetahs are shown to have retractable claws, which cheetahs lack in real-life, as their claws always stick out to provide traction when running. Subverted later in the same episode, when the hyena trio realizes that they've been duped and threaten to eat the two cheetahs as revenge. Also, going by the quotes provided, it is implied that they preyed on a rhino and hippo, both of which are too big and powerful for cheetahs to target in reality.

characters.name: Toucan Dan
characters.description: Toucan Dan is a dangerously clever criminal mastermind toucan who can make anyone believe anything he says. Artistic License – Ornithology: He is able to crush a snail shell with his bill, which is described as being used for "seizing and crushing". In reality, toucan bills are hollow and not strong enough to crush even soft fruit. The "seizing" part is accurate, however. Con Man: He can make anyone believe anything he says with little effort. He once tricked Timon into thinking he'snotToucan Dan, but Santa Claus. Corrupted Character Copy: He's clearly based off ofToucan Sam, but as a notorious criminal instead of a friendly cereal mascot. Feathered Fiend: A toucan who is a criminal mastermind.

characters.name: The Vulture Police
characters.description: The vulture police are a pair of fast-talking buzzards who are policemen of the jungle. Detective Animal: When Timon and Toucan Dan disguise as each other, the vulture police help Pumbaa identify which is which. Police Are Useless: In "Yosemite Remedy", they release a raccoon criminal after he convinced them that he found Timon and Pumbaa's suitcase instead of stealing it, while in reality, he did steal the valuables that were in the suitcase. As a result, Timon decides to take matters into his own hands. They do, however, end up arresting the criminal when they find out he stole Timon and Pumbaa's valuables. Punch-Clock Villain: They're only doing their jobs, but they tend to hinder Timon and Pumbaa more often than they help them out. Vile Vulture: Inverted. They are vultures who are on the side of the law, though they tend to not offer much help to Timon and Pumbaa.

characters.name: Ned the Elephant
characters.description: Ned is a high and mighty elephant who thinks he's wonderful at everything. He seems to enjoy teasing Timon and Pumbaa whenever they try to prove their worth to him. Alpha Bitch: Is the most popular animal in the jungle, according to "Uganda Be An Elephant", but tends to lord it over other animals. Cruel Elephant: Downplayed. Ned is not particularly evil, but he's pompous, arrogant and quick to make fun of those he considers inferior. Fat and Proud: Being an elephant, he’s quite proud of his massive size. When Pumbaa appears before him fattened up from having overeaten to try to emulate his size, Ned ridiculed him for mocking his "majestic bulk". Just Desserts: In his last appearance, he falls into a river and gets eatenby piranhas, an ironic fate for one proud of his bulky size.

characters.name: The Natives
characters.description: The natives are a group of indigenous peoples who live mostly in Bora Bora. They are revealed to be university students looking for a job. Verbal Tic: The chief precedes everything he says with "Bungala Bungala". (i.e. "Bungala bungala, you goofs!")

characters.name: Little Jimmy
characters.description: Little Jimmy is a cute, yet dangerous bluebird. He appears to have two voices: his adorable, innocent voice and his criminal mastermind voice. When he gets turned in by Timon and Pumbaa, he becomes cellmates with Smolder the Bear. Cute Is Evil: At first, he presents himself as a helpless,adorable-looking bluebirdwith an innocent voice. When histrue nature as a criminal mastermindis revealed, he tends to look a bit older. Feathered Fiend: A bluebird who pretends to be helpless and innocent, but is really a criminal mastermind. The Napoleon: He's small and evil. Wounded Gazelle Gambit: He tends to present himself as a helpless little bluebird.

characters.name: Rabbit
characters.description: Rabbit is a large pink bunny who started out as a neutral character, but later became an antagonist. He appears to be annoying, obnoxious, and very tiring to Timon and Pumbaa. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: He's a pink bunny. Gonk: Possibly the most unsavory-looking character in the entireLion Kingfranchise. No Name Given: He's referred to as simply "the rabbit" or just "rabbit". Rabbit Magician: In "Africa Dabra!", he's a magicalReality Warperwho makes his introduction by trying to pull himself out of a hat.

characters.name: Tatiana
characters.description: Tatiana is a meerkat who is the daughter of the Duke meerkat and Timon's former love interest back at the meerkat colony. After being rescued by Timon from a cobra, the two meerkats are about to get married, until the Duke (Tatiana's father) forces Timon to choose between her or Pumbaa. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears a blue hairbow and silver crown. Damsel in Distress: Is kidnapped by a cobra early on, which leads to Timon getting banished from the colony. When she's next seen, she's still in the cobra's clutches, requiring Timon (with Pumbaa's help) to save her. Furry Female Mane: Light blonde hair. Tertiary Sexual Characteristics: Her eyelashes, hair and blue ribbon

characters.name: Sharla
characters.description: Sharla is a warthog who is Pumbaa's former love interest back at the warthog sounder. She and the three male warthogs banished Pumbaa from the group due to his gas odor. Despite that, Sharla still has romantic feelings for the warthog outcast. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: She's pink. Old Flame: To Pumbaa. She still harbours feelings for him even after she banished him from the sounder, and she even offers to take him back in after he risks his life to save the sounder from the guineafowl.

characters.name: Monti
characters.description: Monti is a meerkat who was briefly Pumbaa's new friend in "Kenya Be My Friend?" He is also shown to be the best friend of another warthog named Baampu, whom he hasn't seen in years. Butt Sticker: How does Pumbaa meet him? By sitting on him! Does Not Like Spam: Unlike Timon, he finds grubs revolting, and as he tells Pumbaa, "they give you gas".He prefers fruits, nuts, and soybean products. Meaningful Name: His name is the same as Timon with the two syllables in a different order. Palette Swap: Looks like Timon, but with darker brown fur and blonde hair.

characters.name: Baampu
characters.description: Baampu is a warthog who was briefly Timon's new friend in "Kenya Be My Friend?" He is also shown to be the best friend of another meerkat named Monti, whom he hasn't seen in years. Meaningful Name: Similar Monti, his name is an anagram for Pumbaa. Palette Swap: Looks like Pumbaa, but with dark blue fur and a brown mane. The Quiet One: Relatively, although he is very excited once around his friend Monti. Replacement Goldfish: As mentioned, he briefly becomes Timon's new friend.

characters.name: Pumbaa Jr.
characters.description: Pumbaa Jr. is an alligator who gets raised by Timon and Pumbaa until he finds a female mate and gets sent to a chicken barn. Despite being an alligator, Timon mistakes him to be an "ugly chicken", as he believes thatonlychickens lay eggs. Break the Cutie: He is heartbroken when he overhears Timon saying he is not Pumbaa's child, but an "ugly chicken", and decides to run away from home. Not only Pumbaa becomes devastated when he finds out, but Timonfeels horribly guiltyand agrees they set off to find him. Cheerful Child: Is generally very upbeat and friendly - until he eavesdrops on Timon's hurtful remarks. Face of a Thug: Pumbaa Jr. is a genuinely friendly and innocent child, but heisan alligator. Timon even consistently refers to him as "an ugly chicken". Green Gators: A typically green cartoon alligator.

characters.name: Ralph and Eduardo
characters.description: Ralph and Eduardo "Eddie" are a pair of villainous snakes who create an all-you-can-eat bug buffet in order to capture and eat Timon and Pumbaa. The Ditz: Eddie is clearly not the brains of the outfit - as demonstrated by the above quote, he thought "horseradish" was a horseanda radish separately! Exit, Pursued by a Bear: The two snakes are chased off by a giant, chainsaw-wielding piranha at the end of the episode. Hoist by His Own Petard: As Timon himself puts it, "Two can play that game!" After luring the duo into a fake bug buffet with the intent of fattening them up for dinner, Ralph and Eddie are tricked by Timon and Pumbaa in a similar way with a fake fast food establishment. It's All About Me: Ralph shows traits of this, as he imagines himself as a superhero and a movie star on the red carpet at one point.

characters.name: Nefu
characters.description: Nefu is a young mandrill who is the nephew of Rafiki. His goal is to become a shaman just like his uncle. Punny Name:Nefuis Rafiki'snephew.

characters.name: Leslie Lambeau
characters.description: Leslie Lambeau is a supermodel whom Pumbaa and Bear have romantic feelings for. Expy: She looks a lot like Hello Nurse fromAnimaniacs. Interspecies Romance: She is the object of affection for a warthog and a bear. Timon even lampshades to Pumbaa that they are from two different worlds and two different species. Let's Just Be Friends: She ultimately rejects both Pumbaa and the Bear's advances, saying they should just be friends. Pumbaa understands while the Bear is left a sobbing mess.

characters.name: Pimon and Tumbaa
characters.description: Pimon and Tumbaa are a buff meerkat and warthog duo who are evil counterparts of Timon and Pumbaa. After they steal their bag of bugs, Timon and Pumbaa learn kung-fu from Rafiki so that they can fight them for their food. The Bully: They push around and threaten Timon and Pumbaa. Evil Counterpart: They're basically bigger, meaner versions of Timon and Pumbaa. They even create their own motto, just to mock them. Gag Lips: Tumbaa has a huge lower lip.

characters.name: Dr. Cagliostro
characters.description: Dr. Cagliostro is a mad scientist who appeared in the Season 2 episode "Monster Massachusetts". Amazing Technicolor Population: He's a mad human doctor withgreen skin. Happily Married: He ends up marrying his monster (who had beenturned into a woman) and becoming "the happiest man on Earth". Karma Houdini: Receives no comeuppance for experimenting on Timon and Pumbaa, apart from his assistant Torgo briefly turning against him. Mad Scientist: Exactly like he is, he captures Timon and Pumbaa and experiments on them.

characters.name: Torgo
characters.description: Flesh Golem: What he appears to look like, a nod toFrankenstein's Monster. Gender Bender: Gets transformed from a male monster to an attractive human woman. Happily Married: Gets married to Dr. Cagliostro at the end of the episodein her human form. Karma Houdini: After kidnapping the meerkat and warthog duo and subjecting them to hideous transformations, he ends upTransformed Ever Afterand married to the mad doctor who created him. Vocal Dissonance: Has a rather sophisticated British voice in contrast to his monstrous appearance and speaking in thethird person.

characters.name: Piper
characters.description: A female flying squirrel whom Timon and Pumbaa meet in Saskatchewan. She's infatuated with another flying squirrel, so the duo agree to help arrange a date in exchange for rare beetles. Big Beautiful Woman: A heavy-set female squirrel who is quite attractive. Deadpan Snarker: Her first reaction to Timon and Pumbaa introducing themselves formally is a sarcastic "Yeah, charmed". And she doesn't hold back when Timon annoys her, grabbing him by his collar and snapping at him Single Woman Seeks Good Man: She's infatuated with a male flying squirrel, and only agrees to help the duo if they can arrange a date between them. Tiny Guy, Huge Girl: The huge girl to her crush's tiny guy.

characters.name: Bruce
characters.description: A land crab that Timon encounters in the Australian Outback and tries to catch, believing him to be a huge bug. Awesome Aussie: An Australian land crab that completely wipes the floor with Timon in every encounter. Blood Knight: He enjoys scrapping with Timon so much that he hopes at one point that the meerkat hasn't given up yet. Crazy-Prepared: Whatever Timon tries to catch him with, Bruce is prepared for. Pesticide is met with a gas mask, he claws his way up Timon's mechanical boot from the inside and tricks Timon into falling for his own trap. Giant Enemy Crab: Inverted. He's a giant crab, but he befriends Pumbaa and helps him catch bugs. That said, he constantly battles Timon to the point where the meerkat grows to fear him (but to be fair, Timon was the one antagonizing Bruce in the first place).

characters.name: Lester
characters.description: Father Neptune: Speaks with a deep gravelly voice with typical sailor slang, while also wearing a small sailor cap. Gender-Blender Name: Apparently, Lester had the same name as a princess. Human All Along: Was originally a human princess turned into amaletalking whalethat grants wishes. Noodle Incident: It's never specifiedwhocursed Lester or for what reason. Vocal Dissonance: Retains that same sea captain voiceeven afterturning back into a princess.

characters.name: Cisco Pig
characters.description: The Dreaded: He's so feared that everyone in town flees at the sight of Pumbaa, mistaking him for the criminal. Even his own men flee when he gets mad at them for threatening the main duo. Even Evil Has Standards: Despite being a notorious gunslinger, he highly respects Timon and Pumbaa (his favorite cartoon characters), saving them from his gang and then dancing with them. Not Quite Dead:The episode starts with him apparently being hit by a train he attempted to rob. But he reappears by the end to stop his gang from shooting Timon and Pumbaa. Pig Man: Looks like a cross between a human and a warthog, having a pig-like nose and a large mustache resembling tusks. Solid Cartoon Facial Stubble: Has a dark swath of facial hair below his mustache.

characters.name: Anteater
characters.description: Aardvark Trunks: He's got a flexible trunk with his lips on the end. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: A blue anteater. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Has large, black eyebrows. The Cameo: Aside from his main appearance, he makes a quick cameo in "Congo On Like This" as one of the animals being blown away by Simba's roar.In Africa. Fat Slob: Obese and lazy, he prefers not to hunt and relies ontricking peopleto do the work for him.

characters.name: Bigfoot
characters.description: Big-Hearted Bigfoot: A brown, hairyGentle Giantwho is quick to befriend and play games with anyone he meets. Dumb Muscle: Huge but dimwitted. A prime example is when he hides Timon in a tree and immediately forgets where the meerkat is. Friend to All Living Things: He considers the bugs hovering over his head to be his friends. After Timon and Pumbaa eat them all, he decides to befriendtheminstead, and finally ends upChasing a Butterflyto call his new friend. The Pig-Pen: He's always followed by a swarm of flies. In fact, a big reason Pumbaa looks up to him is because he's filthy, just like Timon and himself.

characters.name: Martin Partin
characters.description: Catchphrase: Says "Oooh, pretty impressive, isn't he?", each time his armadillo does something. Banzai later says this when Partin is being stewed. Gag Nose: Has a nose that's almost the length of his body. Laser-Guided Karma: He spends much of his screen time bullying his cameraman Ronald and shooing away the hyenas whenever they want in on the spotlight. Once his star quits, he finally welcomes the hyenas, who at this point decide to hijack the show and eat him instead, with Ronaldturning on him. Misplaced Wildlife: He comes all the way to Africa to film an armadillo, who was also brought along since they don't live there. Nice Character, Mean Actor: Acts like a cordial nature host on television, but is a jerk towards his staff and anyone who interferes with his filming.
